Premium renewal rate change by line of business for July 2026 highlights include: Looking at the second quarter of 2026, Applied Systems’ Ivans said average premium renewal rate averaged 4.93%, a decrease compared to 5.28% in Q1 2026. However, month over month, commercial auto, business owners policy, general liability, commercial property and umbrella saw a decrease, while workers comp experienced an increase, said Chicago-based Ivans.

item.title: T+1 Settlement: are firms ready for 2027?
item.description: The UK’s move to a T+1 securities settlement cycle on 11 October 2027 is a fundamental shift in how securities transactions are settled. We’ve found that some are more ready than others – and some have a lot to do to meet deadlines, and our expectations. We’re testing how ready market participants are for the transition, and where implementation challenges and bottlenecks remain.

item.title: How A Teenage Carpenter Became The Founder Of AI Construction Startup Trunk Tools
item.description: Before founding Trunk Tools , an AI startup for the construction industry, Sarah Buchner spent more than a decade working in construction. While doing that research, she realized something that would later become central to Trunk Tools: Construction companies produce huge amounts of information, but much of it is fragmented across different systems and buried in documents, making it difficult to analyze. She worked her way up and eventually became a general contractor, managing large construction projects in Europe.

item.title: August 9th – 11th US Midwest SCS outbreak may rank as a top-10 industry loss: Guy Carpenter
item.description: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorm activity that struck the Midwest of the United States earlier this month is seen as having the potential to result in a top-10 severe weather insurance industry loss event, which implies that the cost could be around $5.1 billion or higher to the market, according to broker Guy Carpenter. Guy Carpenter also commented on the potential financial impacts of this severe thunderstorm outbreak in the United States, “Given the severity of winds in the Chicago, Indianapolis, and Columbus, OH metropolitan areas, insured losses are likely to be measured in the billions of dollars.” The broker added: “It is plausible given initial reports of damage that the last several days of severe weather activity could breach the top ten list.” Guy Carpenter’s ranking of the top-10 severe convective storm insured loss events in the United States since 1995 can be seen below: At the bottom of that list is a $5.1 billion industry insured loss event from May 2014. Between August 9th to 11th, the Midwest was impacted by multiple rounds of severe convective storm (SCS) activity, driven by a slow-moving cold front affecting the states of Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Indiana, Ohio, as well as other surrounding states.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re makes sensor-triggered parametric earthquake payout in Peru
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance (LM Re), part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, has issued a parametric payout for the 5.8 magnitude earthquake that struck Peru in May and activated Safehub’s Shake Network trigger. The policy, which is being dubbed by both companies as the world’s first earthquake parametric payment triggered by Safehub’s Shake Network uses ShakeNet Parametric, Liberty Mutual Re’s (LM Re) earthquake parametric solution that is triggered by Safehub’s, a provider of seismic sensor and risk management technology. Powered by the Global Earthquake Model’s (GEM’s) OpenQuake engine, and informed by Safehub’s sensor network, the parametric solution delivers highly localised shaking information that supports rapid, transparent, and objective payouts while enhancing emergency response and post-event decision-making.

item.title: PERILS reduces storm Nils insured market loss estimate to €695m
item.description: Catastrophe data aggregator PERILS has published its third industry loss estimate for extratropical windstorm Nils, also known as “Ulrike”, that struck the Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Occitanie regions in southwest France in mid-February, placing the insurance market loss at €695 million, a notable decline from its second estimate that was published in May. PERILS confirmed that it will provide an updated loss estimate for Nils on February 13th, 2027, twelve months after the event end date. PERILS published its initial insurance industry loss estimate for this windstorm back in March, putting the total at €586 million.

item.title: Accelerant heads back to private ownership with Thoma Bravo acquisition
item.description: Upon completion, Accelerant will become a private company, with its common shares delisted from the New York Stock Exchange, while Altamont Capital Partners, its largest investor, and the firm’s founders intend to retain equity alongside Thoma Bravo, with the terms to be finalised prior to closing. Data-driven risk exchange platform Accelerant has entered into a definitive agreement with Thoma Bravo to become a privately held company in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion. The move marks a strategic return to the private market for Accelerant, highlighting how public markets have at times struggled to properly assess and value tech-enabled, specialty risk exchange platforms over short-term quarters.

item.title: Midwest severe storms could generate billions in insured losses, Guy Carpenter warns
item.description: A severe convective storm outbreak that swept across the US Midwest between August 9 and 11 could generate insured losses running into the billions of dollars, according to a recent report from Guy Carpenter. The firm added, “It is plausible given initial reports of damage that the last several days of severe weather activity could breach the top ten largest US severe convective storm insured losses list.” The latest outbreak follows a substantial severe weather event in the Midwest in late July, which was also identified as having the potential to become a top-10 US severe convective storm insured loss event. “Given the severity of winds in the Chicago, Indianapolis, and Columbus, OH metropolitan areas, insured losses are likely to be measured in the billions of dollars,” Guy Carpenter said.

item.title: LM Re & Safehub make ‘first-of-its-kind’ parametric earthquake payout in Peru
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance Group (LM Re), part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, and Safehub have issued a payout for the magnitude 5.8 earthquake in Peru that triggered Safehub’s Shake Network. The policy, which is being dubbed by the pair as the “world’s first earthquake parametric payment triggered by the Shake Network,” uses ShakeNet Parametric, LM Re’s earthquake parametric solution that is triggered by Safehub’s proprietary sensor network. The speedy payout in Peru demonstrates how the solution can strengthen disaster resilience.” Andy Thompson, Chief Executive Officer, Safehub, added, “A parametric insurance policy is only as good as the data driving the trigger.

item.title: Update: UK Risk Firm Ambrey Working to Salvage Ship Spewing Oil off Omani Coast
item.description: Risk management firm Ambrey said on Thursday it was coordinating the salvage of a ship spilling Russian crude into the Arabian Sea off the coast of Oman in one of the world’s worst oil spills for years. Ambrey has contracted a “leading international oil spill response company” and is working with Oman and other stakeholders to secure the Caroline Bezengi tanker, it said in a statement. An annual monsoon in the area is complicating the salvage efforts, Ambrey said, a day after Oman confirmed that the massive oil slick from the tanker had reached its shores.

item.title: Russia Eyeing Sabotage, Other Attacks in Europe, Officials Warn
item.description: Read more : Germany Sees Russian Covert Attacks as Prelude to Wider Conflict At the same time, it’s also possible Russia merely wants to give the impression it’s considering escalating attacks in Europe to sow fear as part of an information operation, the government official said. Russia may escalate attacks against the Baltic States and Poland, a European intelligence official said, amid rising concern that Moscow wants to further intimidate nations supporting Ukraine. There are indications that Russian intelligence and security services are looking at so-called hybrid warfare operations, which could include infrastructure sabotage or false-flag attacks, the intelligence official said, declining to be named in order to speak freely.

item.title: Low Rhine River Levels Disrupt German Industry
item.description: German companies are reporting growing disruption from Rhine water levels that have hit record lows, with chemical producers, utilities, steelmakers and agricultural traders warning of higher costs, transport bottlenecks and curbed production. “Alarm bells are ringing loudly: the extremely low water levels are increasingly pushing logistics and supply chains to their limits,” Wolfgang Grosse Entrup, CEO of German chemical industry association VCI, told Reuters. Salzgitter, Germany’s second-largest steelmaker, said that the low Rhine levels had forced it to transport coal via train from Rotterdam to its HKM division.

item.title: Sixfold and Sollers partner to accelerate AI underwriting
item.description: Sixfold has partnered with Sollers Consulting to help insurers accelerate underwriting transformation by combining AI-powered risk assessment with insurance consulting and implementation expertise. Sixfold and Sollers will work with insurers to automate submission intake, assess risks against their own underwriting appetite and generate transparent, explainable recommendations within existing systems and workflows. “Sixfold makes submission handling faster, more consistent and more intelligent,” said Jakub Śliwiński, head of underwriting at Sollers.

item.title: Daisy Tsang to co-lead HSBC insurance business
item.description: The bank plans to appoint  Kai Zhang , Asia head of international wealth and premier banking, and  Daisy Tsang , CEO of HSBC Life Hong Kong and Macau, as co-CEOs of the insurance business alongside their existing roles, according to sources. HSBC’s global head of insurance, Edward Moncreiffe, is set to leave the bank in September after two decades with the lender, as the group continues a broader restructuring and focuses on expanding its wealth business in Asia. Moncreiffe, who has led HSBC’s global insurance business since 2024, is leaving for external opportunities, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Big ‘I’ report shows a stabilizing insurance market
item.description: The Big “I” 2026 Market Share Report shows the independent agency channel continues to maintain control in commercial lines while it is also gaining ground in personal lines. As the insurance market continues to stabilize, the next phase of the market will reward independent agencies that can respond quickly as carriers regain confidence and begin competing for business again. Notably, the independent channel ticked up in personal lines: Personal auto grew from 33% to 34% Homeowners’ insurance grew from 50% to 51% Overall, the market is stable and improving.

item.title: Accelerant to be acquired by Thoma Bravo
item.description: Risk exchange platform Accelerant has entered into a definitive agreement with Thoma Bravo to become a privately held company in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion. Returning to private ownership with Thoma Bravo’s technology and software expertise, coupled with its vast financial and strategic resources, will enable us to make investments that further position our unique, data fueled platform to be the rails on which specialty insurance runs.” – Jeff Radke, Chairman and CEO of Accelerant. Under the terms of the agreement, Accelerant Class A and Class B stockholders will receive $20.25 per share in cash, representing a 49% premium to Accelerant’s closing share price on August 12, 2026.

item.title: Volvo launches new telematics app
item.description: Volvo is introducing Safety Coach, a new telematics app that offers drivers driving insights and tips directly through the infotainment screen and the Volvo Cars mobile app. The tips are guided by findings from Volvo’s “decades-worth of real-world safety knowledge and data,” and the app is powered by Cambridge Mobile Telematics. Starting in Sweden and Norway, drivers of most Volvo cars from model year 2020 can soon download the app.

item.title: Tornado Alley Eastward Shift Adding Risk Concerns, Modeler Says
item.description: The peak of tornado season may be behind us, but the eastward expansion of what has been traditionally known as tornado alley into more populated areas may continue raising awareness of the growing insurance risk long for some time. “The tornado alley’s kind of expanding or shifting a bit eastward, and so I think as we think about that from an insurance perspective and think about ‘What does that mean for insurers,’ I think one of the largest concerns is there’s a lot more population as you move eastward,” said Tory Farney, vice president of Verisk Weather Solutions. Increased losses in new areas weren’t from raw tornado counts across the U.S., but from increased risk exposure, according to one industry catastrophe modeler.

item.title: Court Rules Lawsuit Not Allowed for Heat-Stricken Worker Despite Previous Death
item.description: The employer’s “failure to fully implement its heat stress prevention plan may have been negligent, but we cannot say this failure made it substantially certain death or serious injury would occur,” the court said in its Aug. The facts are these, the court explained: The farm worker, Carlos Vargas Moreno, collapsed in a field on July 19, 2022, almost two years to the day after the previous worker had died under similar circumstances. One farm worker died from heat exposure in 2020, resulting in a fine and citation from the U.S.

item.title: USDA Says Argentine Beef That Missed Inspection Is Recalled
item.description: The USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service announced that Florida-based Corte Argentino LLC was recalling several cuts of beef that missed a “reinspection” step when they entered the US. Nearly 30,000 pounds of Argentine beef that wasn’t fully inspected before being distributed in Texas and Florida are being recalled, the US Department of Agriculture said. The recalled beef cuts came in boxes labeled Frigorifico Gorina SAIC, one of Argentina’s top meatpackers.

item.title: CatIQ finalises loss estimate for Hurricane Debby floods in Ontario & Quebec at C$2.80bn
item.description: CatIQ, the Toronto-based independent catastrophe insurance data provider, has published a final insurance industry loss estimate of CAD $2.80 billion from the severe flooding generated by the remnants of Hurricane Debby that impacted Ontario and Quebec between August 9th and 10th, 2024. Moreover, CatIQ’s final loss estimate is also down from its fourth loss estimate of $2.817 billion, which was issued six months after the event. However, this final estimate is still an increase from CatIQ’s third loss estimate of $2.76 billion, which was issued 90 days after the event took place.

item.title: Suncorp’s exec leadership changes to set insurer for next phase of strategy
item.description: Australian insurer Suncorp Group has announced a number of changes to its executive leadership team, including the appointment of Bridget Messer as Chief Executive Customer, Brand and Digital, a newly created role. As a result of these changes, Michelle Bain, currently Executive General Manager of Compulsory Third Party Insurance will join the Executive Leadership Team as Suncorp’s Chief Risk Officer. She will retain accountability for the rollout of Suncorp’s Digital Insurer program.

item.title: Axle secures $17.5m Series A as insurtech company expands automated platform
item.description: Axle, a technology company developing an AI-native clearinghouse for the insurance industry, has raised USD $17.5 million in Series A funding as it expands its platform for automating insurance verification and policy-related processes. “Axle gives us an instant, accurate answer at the moment it matters and has helped us recover millions in losses we used to write off each year.” Axle’s platform is designed to address what the company describes as a fragmented insurance technology infrastructure. Axle said members of the early Plaid team are among its existing investors.

item.title: HIVE Underwriters strengthens cargo division
item.description: Independent specialty MGA HIVE Underwriters has announced the appointment of Polly Mays as Head of Cargo, bringing a decade of experience in the cargo insurance market, and extensive expertise across cargo, stock throughput, excess stock and project cargo risks. Her appointment further strengthens HIVE’s Marine division as the business continues to expand its underwriting capabilities across global specialty markets. HIVE’s Marine division specialises in technically complex marine risks, including Marine Cargo, Marine Liability, Transportation & Logistics, Marine War and Marine Miscellaneous.

item.title: WV Fire Commission Has Failed to Make Plan to Address High Fire Death Rate
item.description: An audit of the State Fire Commission in December of 2025 noted that the commission hadn’t compiled a state-mandated plan to prevent these deaths. When the state fire commission was created in 1976, it was charged with developing a plan for fire prevention and control, which includes assessing manpower needs, location of training centers, location of water sources and public education and information needs. However the past Fire Marshal also agreed to create a plan and address underlying causes behind fatal fires, most of which are residential.

item.title: Atlanta Airport Taps Munis for $1.1 Billion Mega Bond Sale
item.description: The world’s busiest airport is coming to market with a more than $1 billion municipal bond sale, boosting issuance in the lagging airport sector. The jumbo sale, expected to price Tuesday, comes as muni issuance in the airport sector hovers at roughly $10 billion so far this year, about 28% lower than at this point last year. Those mega deals — at or above $1 billion each — made for a blockbuster year for airport issuance with nearly $24 billion sold.

item.title: Homeowners Insurance Market Reaches ‘Fragmented Phase,’ Says S&P GMI
item.description: New research from S&P Global Market Intelligence looks to suggest that homeowners insurers are reaching rate adequacy, but certain marketplace factors are creating what it called a “fragmented phase.” Nationally, the US effective approved homeowners rate change declined from about 13.6% in 2024, to about 6.3% in 2025, to now about 1.8% through July 2026. Homeowners insurers have posted profitable underwriting results thanks to some lighter catastrophe losses, which may reduce the need for rate changes. “The 2026 cycle, therefore, belongs to a fragmented, state by-state answer set built on localized catastrophe experience, regulatory realization, underwriting appetite and earned performance rather than on a uniform national resolution,” said S&P GMI.

item.title: bolt Launches AI Distribution Platform
item.description: (Image source: bolt homepage.) bolt (part of Singapore-based bolttech) has launched an AI-powered insurance distribution platform designed to support distribution partners across lines of business, including admitted, E&S and wholesale markets. The platform is intended to unify customer data, workflows and market access across the insurance distribution lifecycle, according to a bolt statement. bolt describes the platform as part of a connected distribution operating model for revenue growth.

item.title: Capricorn Mutual Goes Live on Duck Creek
item.description: (Image source: Capricorn Mutual homepage.) Capricorn Mutual (Perth, Australia) has gone live on Duck Creek Technologies (Boston), replacing its legacy insurance platform. “By modernising our core systems, we’re building a stronger, more resilient business that can continue to deliver the protection, service and support our Members rely on.” Duck Creek says the implementation provides Capricorn Mutual with a connected, cloud-native foundation that supports automation, stronger governance, improved data quality, operational efficiency and future innovation. “Capricorn Mutual had a clear vision for how technology could support its members and strengthen its business for the future,” comments Christian Erickson, General Manager, APAC, Duck Creek.

item.title: Munich Re posts record first-half profit
item.description: Munich Re reported a first-half net result of €3.9 billion, up from €3.2 billion a year earlier, after generating €2.2 billion in the second quarter. The reinsurer maintained its full-year profit target of €6.3 billion. At the July renewals, Munich Re reduced business volume by 9.1% to €2.9 billion as risk-adjusted prices declined 5.5%.

item.title: Flarre.AI Launches Insurance AI Platform
item.description: The platform combines an insurance knowledge graph, an agent studio, an orchestration layer and prebuilt point solutions, according to a Flarre.AI statement. “Flarre.AI answers all three by design, in a secure environment with the organization’s context encoded in a knowledge graph.” The company says its platform supports more than 25 lines of business across P&C and life/annuity, including auto, property, specialty lines such as D&O and cyber, life insurance, group benefits, disability and retirement products. (Image source: Flarre.AI.) Flarre.AI (Tampa, Fla.) has launched its agentic AI platform for property/casualty and life/annuity insurers.

item.title: Meta, 29 States Head to Court in Biggest Test Yet of Youth Social Media Litigation
item.description: Related: Appeals Court Allows Thousands of Social Media Suits Over User Addiction Claims to Proceed In terms of potential damages and implications for Meta, the trial is the biggest test yet of youth social media litigation and comes amid a broader reckoning across the globe over social media’s effects on young users. Meta Platforms will face a coalition of state attorneys general in a California federal court trial beginning on Wednesday over claims it engineered Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children, a case that could expose the company to massive damages and force it to make sweeping changes to its platforms. The trial in Oakland, expected to last seven weeks, will test Colorado, Kentucky, California and New Jersey’s allegations that Meta designed its platforms to keep young users hooked and misled consumers about their safety.

item.title: FlightAware Sues Kalshi Over Flight-Cancellation Markets
item.description: Flight-tracking service FlightAware is suing prediction markets giant Kalshi accusing the company of using its data and name to run “gambling markets on flight cancellations” without permission. (Reporting by Parashuraman in Bengaluru; Editing by Lincoln Feast.) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Contiguous U.S. Breaks Record for Hottest Month Ever: NOAA
item.description: The contiguous United States sizzled to its hottest month ever last month, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The biggest driver of the record heat was nighttime lows that smashed the old record for hottest minimums by 0.7 degrees, NOAA said. The heat was so widespread that every one of the Lower 48 states was at least 1 degree Fahrenheit (nearly 0.6 degrees Celsius) warmer than the 20th-century average, said Russ Vose, chief of monitoring at NOAA’s National Center for Environmental Information.

item.title: Judge Balks at Holding California Utility Liable for Eaton Wildfire
item.description: Insurance companies lost a bid to hold Edison International’s Southern California utility liable for a massive Los Angeles-area wildfire without a trial. If the judge makes her tentative ruling final, Edison will get a chance to argue to a jury at a trial set for next year that the unusual circumstances around the ignition of the Eaton Fire do not qualify for inverse condemnation — the legal principle under which California property owners can recover their losses without having to prove that a utility acted recklessly. Superior Court Judge Laura Seigle on Tuesday tentatively denied a request to hold Southern California Edison on the hook for billions of dollars in property losses under a state law that holds utilities automatically liable when their equipment starts a fire.

item.title: Insurers Overestimate Their Progress With AI: Study
item.description: A study of more than 300 respondents covering several industries finds a considerable disconnect between how organizations assess their progress on AI and where they actually are with real-world AI integration in the insurance sector. Enterprise AI Study found a significant shift from experimentation to enterprise-wide scale in AI. Scaling AI is now a high priority for 96% of insurers, compared to 86% in 2025.

item.title: Global data centre insurance market projected to exceed $24bn by 2030: Allianz Commercial
item.description: The global data centre insurance market is projected to grow from currently around US $11 billion to more than $24 billion by 2030, which comes as the market continues to drive an influx of infrastructure risks and opportunities, according to Allianz Commercial, the commercial insurance business of Allianz Group. There have been comments made by senior industry leaders that capacity may be insufficient to support all the data centre builds expected to come online over the next few years, with the insurance-linked securities market seen as a viable source of incremental reinsurance capacity to support this. Thomas Lillelund, CEO of Allianz Commercial, commented: “AI is turning the latest generation of data centers from a specialist real estate asset into mission-critical infrastructure.” “The scale of investment is extraordinary and, as these centers evolve beyond traditional data storage to high-performance compute demands, success will increasingly depend on resilience: access to power, reliable supply chains, robust construction controls, as well as climate-aware site selection and insurance programs that reflect the true accumulation risk.

item.title: Arch net property cat premiums fell 27% in H1. CEO says more risk ceded to third-party capital
item.description: Chief Financial Officer, also said, “Turning to the reinsurance segment, net premiums written were down 10.4 percent from the same quarter one year ago, reflecting reduced ratings from lower rates and a higher level of retrocession purchases, primarily in the specialty and property catastrophe lines.” In recent months we’ve had more evidence of Arch’s continuing third-party capital partnership initiatives, as well as its appetite for retrocession. Over the first-half of 2026, Bermuda headquartered re/insurer Arch Capital reported a 27% reduction in net property catastrophe reinsurance premiums, while its senior executives noted higher cessions to reinsurance (likely retro) and third-party capital providers. Arch Capital appears to be demonstrating cycle management here, in opting to leverage its diversified platform and access to retrocessional and third-party capital to support a reduction in net property catastrophe premiums at a time when the market has softened.

item.title: Lincoln Financial appoints Adam Cohen as Interim CFO
item.description: Lincoln Financial, a US financial services company specialising in insurance, retirement and wealth management products, has announced the appointment of Adam Cohen, Chief Accounting Officer and Treasurer, as Interim Chief Financial Officer. Lincoln will conduct a comprehensive search process to identify its permanent Chief Financial Officer, including consideration of both internal and external candidates. Cohen joined Lincoln in 2022 as Chief Accounting Officer and assumed responsibility for Treasury in 2024.

item.title: Amynta to acquire agricultural industry specialist MGU Southern States Underwriters
item.description: Insurance services provider Amynta Group has agreed to acquire Southern States Underwriters and SSC Insurance Agency (collectively, Southern States Underwriters), the insurance operations of Southern States Cooperative, Inc. A managing general underwriter (MGU) founded in 1953 and based in Richmond, Virginia, Southern States Underwriters provides commercial property and casualty insurance to meet the specialised needs of suppliers, distributors, and service providers for the agricultural industry. Commenting on the deal, Robert Giammarco, Chairman and CEO of Amynta Group, said: “Southern States Underwriters is a well-established and respected business, dedicated to serving the agribusiness market for over 70 years.

item.title: Norman joins Gallagher Re as Divisional Director within its Facultative team
item.description: Gallagher Re, a global reinsurance brokerage and advisory firm, has announced the appointment of Jenna Norman as Divisional Director, Fac. Norman is joining Gallagher Re from WTW, where she most recently served as Reinsurance Broker within the London Market Retro team. Norman brings extensive expertise in Facultative property broking, specialising in Facultative property broking, working extensively on complex property reinsurance placements for both UK and US clients.

item.title: People Moves: IMA Expands Private Equity and M&A Practice
item.description: IMA Financial Group announced the addition of seven new hires to its Private Equity and M&A Practice. Less than five years after its launch, the Private Equity practice includes 50 associates serving more than 350 private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies, supporting $8.4 billion in annual transaction volume. The practice also includes IMA Diligence Services , IMA’s Chicago-based financial due diligence business, providing financial and lender due diligence and transaction advisory services to private equity firms, commercial lenders and institutional investors.

item.title: Washington University in St. Louis Sued for Retaliation
item.description: Louis is being sued for allegedly violating federal law by firing an employee in retaliation for her opposition to race discrimination and filing a discrimination charge with the U.S. According to the suit, Amega Thaier, who worked as a senior program manager at Washington University’s Alvin J. Siteman Cancer Center, complained to both the university and the EEOC that she was separated from her colleagues because of her race during a mandatory training session provided by the University’s Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.
